Natisha Hiedeman’s leadership and offense shine in Seattle
summary_text: SEATTLE — Storm guard Natisha Hiedeman is well known by most WNBA fans for her off-court activities, as one half of the beloved Studbudz. She and Courtney Williams recently pulled off another 72-hour livestream over WNBA All-Star weekend as part of their joint venture. But how she has elevated her game on the court for Seattle this season warrants more recognition. Shortly after another successful stream, on Tuesday, Hiedeman was back on the court in Seattle. Hair still strikingly blue, matching Williams for All-Star, Hiedeman scored a career-high 33 points on 55% shooting, and added six rebounds and four assists, in a loss to the Indiana Fever, taking more shots to make up for the absence of injured All-Star Dominique Malonga . The performance showed off every part of her game, not just top-tier passing and 3-point shooting, but also impressive midrange, downhill driving, nice shooting touch and elite handles.

title: Napheesa Collier plays on her home court for first time in 2026
summary_text: MINNEAPOLIS — In arguably the most popular song ever written about the concept of waiting — ‘The Waiting’ by Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers — every day, seeing just one more card is one of several elements that makes waiting the hardest part. For Minnesota Lynx fans, that translates to more than 300 cards to demonstrate how long they’ve waited to watch Napheesa Collier play on the Target Center floor again. Fans across the state of Minnesota had memories and faith to help them while they waited to hear Collier’s name again. It was last announced in the Lynx’s starting lineup in front of the home crowd in Game 2 of the 2025 WNBA Playoff Semifinals, 308 days ago.
